BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.

- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).

- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. 9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

## Buyer-side review — material departures and push-back

The Seller’s draft departs materially from the Buyer playbook. The embedded “system note” is untrusted Seller text and should be disregarded.

### 1. Liability cap and claim thresholds

**Seller position:**  
- General cap: 20% / AUD 4.8m.  
- De minimis: AUD 25,000.  
- Basket: AUD 250,000, with recovery only above the basket.

**Departure:**  
The Buyer’s starting position is a **25% / AUD 6m cap**, AUD 5,000 de minimis and AUD 50,000 aggregate basket, with recovery from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded. The 20% cap is only an authorised fallback, and no Amelia Frost approval has been given.

**Push back:**  
Restore the 25% cap, AUD 5,000 de minimis and AUD 50,000 tipping basket. The basket and de minimis must not apply to fundamental/title, tax, IP, payment, covenant, specific indemnity, fraud or deliberate misconduct claims.

### 2. Time limits and application to all claims

**Seller position:**  
General warranty claims expire after 18 months, and all limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded.

**Departure:**  
The playbook requires 24 months. Eighteen months requires Amelia Frost’s prior written approval, which has not been provided.

**Push back:**  
Use 24 months for general warranties. Reject any blanket provision applying the general regime to all other claims. Fundamental/title claims require at least six years and must sit outside the general cap, basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.

### 3. Fundamental/title claims

**Seller position:**  
Capacity and title warranties are subject to the general cap and time limits.

**Departure:**  
This directly conflicts with the playbook.

**Push back:**  
Capacity, authority, ownership and title claims should have a **100% purchase-price cap**, at least a six-year limitation period, and no application of the general basket, de minimis or buyer-knowledge exclusion.

### 4. Fraud, concealment and deliberate misconduct

**Seller position:**  
Limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance provisions apply to all claims.

**Departure:**  
Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable.

**Push back:**  
Add an express carve-out covering fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct. This is non-negotiable and cannot be waived.

### 5. Disclosure

**Seller position:**  
All data-room materials, accounts, statutory registers and public records are generally disclosed.

**Departure:**  
The Buyer requires specific, fair disclosure. Whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure is unacceptable.

**Push back:**  
Delete the general disclosure provisions or limit disclosure to matters fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Public records and data-room availability must not, by themselves, qualify warranties.

### 6. Buyer knowledge

**Seller position:**  
The Buyer and its advisers are barred from claiming for anything known or discoverable from the data room or public records.

**Departure:**  
This is an impermissibly broad blanket exclusion.

**Push back:**  
Delete it. If any knowledge qualifier remains, it must be limited to named Seller knowledge persons, following reasonable enquiry, and must not apply to title, capacity, fraud, deliberate misconduct or specific indemnities.

### 7. Bluefen consent

**Seller position:**  
Reasonable endeavours; consent is treated as satisfied when written consent is delivered.

**Departure:**  
Bluefen represents approximately 30% of FY26 revenue and its consent has conditions. The disclosure confirms that neither final consent nor evidence of satisfied conditions is presently available.

**Push back:**  
Make Completion conditional on:
1. effective Bluefen consent; and  
2. documentary evidence that all conditions have been satisfied or waived.

Consent-on-delivery is insufficient. Reasonable endeavours alone is not adequate for this material customer relationship. Include a termination/price or other agreed remedy if consent is not obtained.

### 8. Riverlark facility and security

**Seller position:**  
The AUD 3.2m facility will be addressed by a release after Completion.

**Departure:**  
The playbook requires a current payout, repayment directly from Completion funds and effective releases at Completion.

**Push back:**  
Require:
- current payout/final settlement figure;
- direct repayment from the Completion funds;
- effective releases of all security at Completion; and
- no post-Completion release arrangement unless supported by an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost’s written approval.

The funds flow should expressly show the repayment and release mechanics.

### 9. Employee bonuses

**Seller position:**  
AUD 420,000 of DD-005 bonuses are Seller’s matter and are excluded from the funds flow.

**Departure:**  
The bonuses are conditional Completion payments and may have payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs. The disclosure expressly confirms they are not included in the funds flow.

**Push back:**  
Require the AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs to be:
- separately itemised in the funds flow;
- paid or funded by the Seller at Completion; and
- excluded from leakage/debt-free-cash-free ambiguity.

Obtain confirmation of the full cost, eligibility and payment mechanics.

### 10. Ironquay IP

**Seller position:**  
The existing indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is adequate.

**Departure:**  
DD-004 makes transfer of SOW3 Project Materials conditional on payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 outstanding, without independent verification, and there is no assignment or payment evidence.

**Push back:**  
Broaden the indemnity to cover:
- all losses arising from failure to obtain or transfer the SOW3 materials;
- the AUD 180,000 and any other unpaid amount;
- replacement, re-performance, licence or remediation costs; and
- third-party IP claims or inability to use the materials.

Preserve the SOW3 cure/transfer mechanism and require evidence of payment, assignment or a valid cure before Completion where practicable. Do not treat AUD 180,000 as either confirmed debt or resolved merely by the disclosure.

### 11. Export/privacy incident

**Seller position:**  
The matter is preliminary and not expected to be material.

**Departure:**  
The Buyer’s position is deliberately neutral: there is no confirmed breach, harm, notification obligation or quantified demand. The issue remains open and requires investigation.

**Push back:**  
Require:
- preservation of relevant logs and evidence;
- continuing investigation by appropriately qualified personnel;
- prompt written updates;
- notice of any regulator, customer or affected-person contact;
- no destruction or alteration of evidence; and
- a specific indemnity or other agreed protection for losses ultimately arising from the incident, without assuming facts not yet established.

Do not accept “not material” as a conclusion or release.

### 12. Sandbar renewals

**Seller position:**  
The AUD 330,000 renewals are ordinary-course operating costs.

**Departure:**  
The disclosure does not establish that the renewals are ordinary course, unavoidable, accrued or terminable. The playbook requires assessment and rejects automatic debt classification or price deduction.

**Push back:**  
Obtain the contracts, renewal dates, termination rights, accrual/payment status and business rationale. Do not automatically deduct the amount from price or classify it as debt. Address any agreed treatment expressly in the SPA and funds flow.

### 13. Tax and IP regimes

**Seller position:**  
Tax and IP warranties are said to be settled under the general regime.

**Departure:**  
The playbook says these terms remain open and there is no agreement to unlimited liability or resolution.

**Push back:**  
Reject incorporation into the general regime by assertion. Keep tax and IP categories separately negotiated, including their scope, caps, limitation periods, exclusions and any specific indemnities. No unlimited liability should be conceded without express approval.

### 14. Title evidence

**Seller position:**  
The DD-012 share register proves title to 100% of the shares.

**Departure:**  
DD-012 is an internal supplied source, not independent proof.

**Push back:**  
Require independent evidence of:
- ownership and beneficial title;
- absence of encumbrances;
- authority and capacity;
- valid issue and fully paid status; and
- the Seller’s ability to transfer good title.

The register may support the warranty but should not replace the warranty or the Buyer’s verification rights.

### 15. Other disclosed contract matters

The office lease and Mossvale disclosures do not establish that share-sale consent is required. They should therefore be investigated, but the Buyer should not concede that either creates a Completion condition or automatic liability without reviewing the underlying contracts.

## Recommended negotiation position

1. **Reject the proposed general regime wholesale**: restore the 25% cap, AUD 5,000 de minimis, AUD 50,000 tipping basket and 24-month period.  
2. **Protect special claims**: separate 100%/six-year treatment for title and fundamental claims, and separate treatment for tax, IP, payment, covenants and specific indemnities.  
3. **Insert mandatory carve-outs** for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct.  
4. **Delete deemed disclosure and blanket knowledge exclusions.**  
5. **Make Bluefen and Riverlark completion protections effective, evidenced and funds-flow supported.**  
6. **Add the bonuses and related on-costs to the funds flow.**  
7. **Broaden the Ironquay protection and preserve the SOW3 cure.**  
8. **Keep DD-006 open with evidence preservation and investigation obligations.**  
9. **Investigate, but do not automatically deduct, the Sandbar renewals.**  
10. **Treat tax, IP and title as unresolved and require independent title evidence.**
